title: History-Learning Frontiers for Longitudinal Incremental Propensity Interventions over Growing Horizons
banked_reason: The proposed all-(n,T,c) matched frontier has been replaced by a long-history theorem plus an explicitly unresolved elbow, so no all-sample evaluable r/ell or complete consistency-and-oracle phase diagram is delivered.
gap_reasons: The proposed all-(n,T,c) matched frontier has been replaced by a long-history theorem plus an explicitly unresolved elbow, so no all-sample evaluable r/ell or complete consistency-and-oracle phase diagram is delivered.

The unresolved kernel is the factor-two logarithmic elbow between the full-prefix plug-in scale and the collision lower scale; explicit compatible-prefix coefficients, a nested-count covariance theorem, and fixed-sample legal-subtree priors are still needed.
D0.5.G assessed tier incremental against floor field, with paper-score ceiling 5.5 below the field ceiling 7.2 and salvageable=false.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery verified the complementary-context lower construction, stable-weight and local-gradient controls, a total truncated-prefix estimator, every-depth risk and honest-length envelopes, and a matched long-history regime. Two targeted D0 rounds strengthened and synchronized that sound package, but the full compatible-prefix approximation remained unavailable because nested prefix counts share descendants and obey parent-sum constraints. The validity gate confirmed that leaving this factor-two logarithmic elbow open substitutes a partial frontier for the promised all-(n,T,c) kernel, so the run terminates as failed rather than narrowing after the fact.
tldr: Longitudinal incremental interventions retain bounded oracle likelihood-ratio variance when the per-period log-odds shift is \(c/\sqrt T\), but this local stability need not control the global cost of learning an unrestricted exponentially branching propensity tree. The paper proves exact finite-tree identification, a dimension-free local efficiency bound, computable truncated-prefix upper envelopes and every-depth collision converses, and the matched long-history frontier \(R(n,T,c)\asymp\min\{1,n^{-1}+c^2\}\) and \(L(n,T,c)\asymp\min\{1,n^{-1/2}+c\}\) once \(T\geq2k_n\). The unresolved kernel is the factor-two logarithmic elbow: a compatible-prefix polynomial approximation, a nested-count variance theorem, and legal-subtree testing priors are still needed for matching all-sample functions and the complete consistency and oracle-penalty phase diagram.
gap: Kim, Kennedy, and Naimi derive identification, efficient influence functions, and nuisance-controlled fixed-horizon inference, but their growing-horizon theorem is a constant-propensity variance comparison. Natural-policy efficiency theory remains local, while bandit and high-dimensional discrete minimax results flatten the data into unrelated one-stage cells and do not contain endogenous products of compatible prefix ratios.
fill: The paper isolates the first mixed-prefix correction, constructs an occupancy-adaptive polynomial or factorial estimator on the original trajectory experiment, calibrates a bias-aware honest connected interval, proves matching all-procedure converses, and evaluates the resulting finite optimization into explicit functions of \(n,T,c\).
